rationale: A wins because it knows when to stop: three real angles, three different protagonists, and proof demands sharp enough to save a founder from pitching vapor. Its “Linear is betting it can grow into product teams without a sales team” correctly treats the missing sales-team fact as a question to verify, while B’s “product managers too” angle calls Linear “engineering-only,” which the update did not say. B also pads the room with “Another roadmapping tool arrives for product teams already drowning in software,” a trend story built on tooling-fatigue color that was never supplied.
gaps_in_A: “The prevailing belief in that beat is that moving from a single-function tool to a cross-functional platform requires enterprise sales headcount and marketing spend” is plausible, but it needs external validation before pitching as a beat premise.

“the launch is live today, 2026-06-09” is inferred from current time, not explicitly stated as launch-day language in the update; acceptable, but should be handled as the company’s stated launch timing.
The first angle leans on “category-creation,” but the update gives product expansion more than a true new-category claim.
gaps_in_B: “engineering-only interface” overstates the facts; the update says Linear is expanding beyond engineering teams, not that the interface was engineering-only.
“historically sold top-down to VPs” is invented market color. No buyer history or VP sales motion appears in the update.
“Another roadmapping tool arrives for product teams already drowning in software” imports a tooling-fatigue trend the update never supplied.
The third and fourth kept angles are padded cousins: “product-management turf” and “another roadmapping tool” both ask whether Linear is one more PM tool without enough new protagonist or proof.
